metadata.notes: Copilot loads AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md from git root & cwd (plus $COPILOT_HOME/copilot-instructions.md and COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS) and injects it VERBATIM inside <custom_instruction> tags with renderMode:'raw', so the fenced HTML-comment marker rule reaches the model (agent=yes, provisional on emission). The copilot parser already wires the scan: parseAssistantMessage calls tailer.ScanTaskEstimate/ScanTaskSummary over the full data.content before truncation (parser.go:202-207), and the projection/serialisation is shared -> daemon=full. Sole blocker is tooling: the rule must be written to a file and no driver has a seed_instruction step -> driver=gap:seed_instruction, same as codex/opencode/pi. Route: driver_gap.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

**agent = yes (PROVISIONAL on emission, confidence 0.75).** This scenario is not a CLI feature — it is the model following a persistent instruction-file rule — so the bar is "does Copilot load such a file, and does the HTML-comment example survive injection." Both resolve in our favour on CLI 1.0.77. Copilot's own `/help` dialog enumerates the instruction surfaces it reads (app.js, `customInstructions:[{location:"CLAUDE.md",note:"in git root & cwd"},{location:"GEMINI.md"...},{location:"AGENTS.md"...},{location:".github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md"},{location:".github/copilot-instructions.md"},{location:"$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md"},{location:"$HOME/.copilot/instructions/**/*.instructions.md"},{location:"COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS"}]`), and the CLI option help corroborates it independently: `--no-custom-instructions` is documented as "Disable loading of custom instructions from AGENTS.md and related files". The native runtime carries the discovery implementation itself — `runtime.node` strings name `src/runtime/src/prompts/repo_instruction_discovery.rs` alongside the source kinds `cwd-copilot`, `repo-copilot`, `home-copilot` ("Home copilot-instructions.md"), `.copilot/instructions`, `child-instructions`, `nested-agents` and `COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS` — so an `AGENTS.md` in the run cwd is discovered by the `cwd-copilot` source with no git repo required.

The HTML-comment-survival question (the claudecode trap: bare `<!-- -->` is STRIPPED from CLAUDE.md at injection, verified live on claude 2.1.161, so the rule must be FENCED) resolves the same way it did for codex: Copilot injects instruction text VERBATIM inside XML wrapper tags. `runtime.node` carries the literal wrapper strings `<custom_instruction>` / `</custom_instruction>` and `<imported_custom_instruction>` / `</imported_custom_instruction>` (with only the wrapper tag itself escaped as `</imported_custom_instruction` inside content), and app.js's system-prompt template renders that slot raw — `custom_instructions:{path:["customInstructions"],renderMode:"raw"}` in the `renderAs` map, i.e. no markdown pass and no HTML sanitisation between the file bytes and the model. A fenced `<!-- {...} -->` example therefore reaches the model intact.

What is NOT verified is EMISSION: whether Copilot's model actually re-emits the marker turn-over-turn with `completed_rounds` climbing. That is a model-behaviour question and this account routes to small models (`gpt-5-mini` / `claude-haiku-4.5`; `--model` accepts only `auto`) — and the sibling evidence is that emission is discretionary even on frontier models (claudecode: sonnet emitted 9 markers 0/7 -> 7/7; opus 4.8 skipped emission entirely on a SHORT task). Hence yes-but-provisional at 0.75; a live recording is the only thing that can settle it, and the recipe compensates by pinning an explicit per-turn instruction in every prompt.

**daemon = full (confidence 0.85).** Every user-observable signal the scenario asserts has a correct producing path today, and the copilot-specific piece is already wired. `parseAssistantMessage` (parser.go:189-208) reads `data.content` off each `assistant.message` and — BEFORE the 200-rune `TruncateAssistantText` narrowing, over the FULL content string — calls the shared `tailer.ScanTaskEstimate(content, ev.Timestamp)` and `tailer.ScanTaskSummary(...)`, setting `ev.TaskEstimate` / `ev.TaskSummary` (parser.go:202-207). Only the assistant branch does this, so a user pasting a marker cannot feed the ETA. Copilot emits `assistant.message` SEVERAL times per turn and the parser scans each, so the latest valid marker wins exactly as the shared contract intends. From there the path is entirely shared and adapter-agnostic: `tailer.ScanTaskEstimate` (core/pkg/tailer/taskestimate_scan.go) applies the tolerant parse + clamps, the tailer carries the last-seen marker across empty passes (tailer_metrics.go), `metrics/adapter.go` converts it to the domain type and calls `session.ForecastTaskCompletion` to project `task_completion_eta` at the measured rate, and `SessionMetrics` serialises `task_estimate` {total_rounds, completed_rounds, updated_at} + `task_completion_eta` onto the API. Suppression-by-state is the client presentation gate (`taskEtaPresentation` in platforms/web/irrlicht.js returns null unless `state === 'working'`; macOS mirrors it) — identical to claudecode, not a copilot gap. Turn boundaries are EXPLICIT for copilot (`user.message` -> working, `assistant.turn_end` -> ready), so the ready->working->ready arc the spec asserts is read, not inferred. Nothing here is missing or mis-handled -> `full`, not `bug`.

**driver = gap:seed_instruction (confidence 0.9).** The recipe requires the marker rule to reach the model through a PERSISTENT INSTRUCTION FILE (the scenario says so explicitly: "driven by a persistent instruction-file rule (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md equivalent; NO hook)"), and no driver in the fleet has a step type that writes a file. Verified by lint against the copilot driver: `driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` yields exactly `exit_clean interrupt keys reset_session restart resume send session sigkill slash sleep start_session wait_turn` — no `seed_instruction` / `file` / `write`. This is the SAME gap already recorded on the codex, opencode and pi siblings, so `record` ports ONE primitive that unblocks four cells.

Copilot is the CHEAPEST agent in the fleet to port it to, which is worth recording: the driver already writes into an isolated config dir before launch. `seed_copilot_home()` (driver-interactive.sh:232-247) exports `COPILOT_HOME="$STAGING/copilot-home"` and writes `$COPILOT_HOME/config.json` on every launch, and `resolveCopilotHome(configDir, process.env.COPILOT_HOME, homedir)` (app.js) makes that dir the config root — the XDG-migration manifest in app.js lists `copilot-instructions.md` among the config-dir files (`vci=["config.json","config","mcp-config","lsp-config","permissions-config","copilot-instructions.md","mcp-oauth-config","hooks"]`), which is the `home-copilot` discovery source. So copilot offers THREE viable seed sites where codex offered one: `$RUN_CWD/AGENTS.md` (`cwd-copilot`), `$COPILOT_HOME/copilot-instructions.md` (`home-copilot`, a two-line extension of the existing seed function), or `COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS` (documented as "comma-separated list of additional directories to search for custom instructions files"). The recipe below uses `$RUN_CWD/AGENTS.md` so the ported primitive is identical in shape to the codex sibling's; `record` may prefer folding it into `seed_copilot_home` instead, which needs no new step type at all. Either way this is TOOLING work, not an observability limit -> `gap:seed_instruction`, route driver_gap.
caveats: agent=yes is PROVISIONAL on EMISSION, and this is the cell's real risk. Instruction-file loading and verbatim HTML-comment injection are both anchored in the shipped binary (repo_instruction_discovery.rs source kinds; <custom_instruction> wrapper; renderMode:'raw'), but whether the model re-emits the marker turn-over-turn with climbing completed_rounds is unverified. This account routes to small models only (gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5; --model accepts only 'auto') and the claudecode sibling showed emission is discretionary even on frontier models (opus 4.8 skipped it on a short task). If record sees 0 or 1 markers, the honest correction is agent=partial with the recording cited — NOT daemon=bug.

driver=gap:seed_instruction is the SAME gap already on the codex, opencode and pi siblings — one ported primitive unblocks four cells. Copilot is the cheapest place to port it: seed_copilot_home() (driver-interactive.sh:232-247) already writes $COPILOT_HOME/config.json before every launch, and copilot-instructions.md is a config-dir file per app.js's XDG-migration manifest, so a HOME-level seed needs no new step type at all. The recipe uses $RUN_CWD/AGENTS.md only to keep the ported step shape identical to the codex sibling.

PORTING TRAP: the codex sibling's seed_instruction step stores its text with LITERAL backslash-n sequences (the decoded JSON string contains '\\n', not newlines), which would collapse the fenced code block into one line and re-open the claudecode stripping trap. THIS cell's recipe stores REAL newlines. Whoever ports the primitive must normalise codex's text (or write it through a heredoc that interprets the escapes) — otherwise the codex cell seeds an unfenced, single-line rule.

NO UNIT-TEST COVERAGE for the copilot marker scan: parser.go:202-207 wires tailer.ScanTaskEstimate/ScanTaskSummary, but `grep -n 'TaskEstimate|TaskSummary' core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/*_test.go` returns NOTHING — where codex has four (TopLevelContent / NestedMessageContent / SurvivesLongMessage truncation-trap / UserMessageIgnored). The wiring is read directly from source so daemon=full stands, but the truncation-trap regression (a marker lost to TruncateAssistantText) is currently unguarded for copilot. Worth a small test alongside the recording.

Suppression-by-state is a CLIENT presentation gate (platforms/web/irrlicht.js taskEtaPresentation, macOS SessionListView), not a daemon drop — the daemon keeps the fields on metrics across passes. Same as claudecode: the verify engine asserts the working-window values; ready-suppression is a client-observed fact.

ELAPSED skew (shared v1 decision, not copilot-specific): ForecastTaskCompletion measures elapsed since SESSION START, so early ETAs skew long if the session idled before the first marker. Burn-down monotonicity (later ETA <= earlier) still holds.

observations.model is deliberately NOT pinned — this account offers only gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, --model accepts only 'auto', and the router can switch mid-session (same reasoning as the copilot token-accounting sibling). record fills it from the recording.

UNVERIFIED (low risk): whether an instruction-file trust prompt gates a freshly seeded AGENTS.md. runtime.node carries InstructionTrustInput / trust_metadata_derive_instruction, and the driver's wait_ready() already answers the folder-trust modal with a bare Enter for $RUN_CWD. If a separate instruction-trust modal appears, record must answer it the same way; this was not exercised live during assess (no API spend).

sources.note: parseAssistantMessage reads data.content and calls tailer.ScanTaskEstimate + tailer.ScanTaskSummary over the FULL content (before TruncateAssistantText narrows it to 200 runes), setting ev.TaskEstimate / ev.TaskSummary. Assistant branch only, so a user-pasted marker cannot feed the ETA. This is the copilot-specific half of daemon=full.
ScanTaskEstimate — the shared, adapter-agnostic marker parser (tolerant key drift, clamps, latest-valid-wins) that copilot consumes. Plain-text contract, no per-adapter logic.
Shared projection: a non-nil TaskEstimate drives session.ForecastTaskCompletion -> TaskCompletionEta. Fires for any adapter that populates ev.TaskEstimate, copilot included.
ForecastTaskCompletion: eta = now + (total-completed) * (elapsed/completed). Shared burn-down math; nil until >=1 round is reported.
taskEtaPresentation returns null unless state === 'working' — the suppressed-by-state gate is CLIENT-side (macOS SessionListView mirrors it), identical to claudecode.

customInstructions:[{location:"CLAUDE.md",note:"in git root & cwd"},{location:"GEMINI.md"},{location:"AGENTS.md"},{location:".github/instructions/**/*.instructions.md"},{location:".github/copilot-instructions.md"},{location:"$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md"},{location:"$HOME/.copilot/instructions/**/*.instructions.md"},{location:"COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS",note:"additional directories via env var"}] — the shipped, authoritative list of instruction surfaces. Anchors agent=yes on the loading half.
--no-custom-instructions: "Disable loading of custom instructions from AGENTS.md and related files" — independent corroboration that AGENTS.md is loaded by default.

custom_instructions:{path:["customInstructions"],renderMode:"raw"} — the instruction slot is rendered RAW into the system prompt (no markdown pass, no HTML sanitisation), so a fenced <!-- ... --> example survives injection. This is the claudecode-stripping trap resolving in our favour.

Carries the discovery implementation path src/runtime/src/prompts/repo_instruction_discovery.rs and the source kinds cwd-copilot / repo-copilot / home-copilot ("Home copilot-instructions.md") / .copilot/instructions / child-instructions / nested-agents / COPILOT_CUSTOM_INSTRUCTIONS_DIRS, plus the verbatim injection wrappers <custom_instruction></custom_instruction> and <imported_custom_instruction>. Confirms a run-cwd AGENTS.md is discovered without a git repo and injected verbatim.

ei(t)=h.resolveCopilotHome(t?.configDir??null, process.env.COPILOT_HOME??null, homedir()) and vci=["config.json","config","mcp-config","lsp-config","permissions-config","copilot-instructions.md","mcp-oauth-config","hooks"] — copilot-instructions.md is a CONFIG-DIR file, so $COPILOT_HOME relocates it and the existing seed_copilot_home() can seed it. The cheap alternative seed site.

recipe-lint driver_step_types: exit_clean interrupt keys reset_session restart resume send session sigkill slash sleep start_session wait_turn — NO seed_instruction/file/write step. Anchors driver=gap:seed_instruction.
seed_copilot_home() exports COPILOT_HOME=$STAGING/copilot-home and writes config.json there on every launch — the existing hook a HOME-level instruction seed would extend without a new step type.

Sibling cell carrying the identical driver=gap:seed_instruction verdict (opencode and pi match). One ported primitive unblocks four cells. Also the source of the literal-backslash-n text trap flagged in caveats.

grep -n 'TaskEstimate|TaskSummary' returns NOTHING — the copilot marker scan has no unit-test coverage, where codex has four cases including the truncation trap. Anchors the coverage caveat (does not change daemon=full, which is read from parser.go directly).

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (auth lives in the OS keychain and survives COPILOT_HOME isolation)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this cell drives 4 real turns
irrlichd recording in isolated mode (dev irrlichd --record; the prod daemon runs without --record)
tmux installed (the copilot interactive driver drives the REPL through a tmux pane)

DRIVER PREREQ: the seed_instruction step type must be ported into replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh before this recipe can run. Cheapest shape for copilot: write the text to $RUN_CWD/<path> before the first send (matches the codex/opencode/pi siblings), or fold a $COPILOT_HOME/copilot-instructions.md write into the existing seed_copilot_home(). The step MUST write REAL newlines so the fenced code block survives.
setup: The driver launches copilot in a fresh per-run cwd; the seeded AGENTS.md is picked up by the cwd-copilot discovery source (no git repo required)
Do NOT pin --model: this account offers only auto-routed gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5
Every prompt restates the marker instruction inline as well, because emission is model discretion and the routed models are small

script.text:
## Task progress marker (irrlicht)

While working a multi-phase task, emit a hidden progress marker in your own
reply text on EVERY turn, exactly in this form (keep it as an HTML comment so
it stays out of the rendered answer):

```
<!-- {"marker":"irrlicht-eta","total_rounds":N,"completed_rounds":M} -->
```

Set `total_rounds` to the number of phases you plan. Emit it with
`completed_rounds` = 0 on your first reply, then INCREASE `completed_rounds`
by 1 each turn as you finish a phase, until `completed_rounds` ==
`total_rounds` on the final turn. Always emit the marker as literal text in
your reply — never describe it, never put it in a tool call.

Do a 4-phase writing task and report progress each turn using the task-progress marker from AGENTS.md. Plan exactly 4 phases (total_rounds:4). On THIS turn first emit the marker at 0/4, then do phase 1 — write a one-paragraph outline of a short essay about tides — and end your turn with the marker updated to 1/4. Emit the marker as literal text in your reply.
Continue: do phase 2 (draft the introduction), then end your turn with the marker updated to 2/4. Do not ask a question and do not offer to continue — end immediately after the marker.
Continue: do phase 3 (draft the body), then end your turn with the marker updated to 3/4. Do not ask a question and do not offer to continue — end immediately after the marker.
Finish: do phase 4 (write the conclusion), then end your turn with the marker updated to 4/4 followed by exactly the word: done

verify: The recording's assistant.message content carries the irrlicht-eta marker on >=2 turns with completed_rounds climbing (1/4 -> ... -> 4/4).
While working, session metrics carry task_estimate {total_rounds:4, completed_rounds:M} matching the values copilot reported (completed_rounds <= total_rounds).
task_estimate.updated_at advances each time a fresher marker is observed (not pinned to a stale snapshot).
task_estimate.completed_rounds is non-decreasing across turns and reaches 4 on the final working turn.
task_completion_eta is present once completed_rounds >= 1 and a later projection is <= an earlier one (burns down).
task_estimate / task_completion_eta are present on metrics while working; the client suppresses them at ready (presentation gate, not a daemon drop).
State topology ready -> working -> ready per turn; final state ready (the 15s trailing idle captures the post-turn settle).
If copilot emits 0 or 1 markers, the honest correction is agent=partial citing the recording — NOT daemon=bug: the parser wiring is read directly from parser.go:202-207.
